# The Weyl group is generated by simple reflections

`Langlands.Group.exists_list_prod_ofIdx_baseOf` proves the following. Let
`R` be a linearly ordered field (`[Field R] [LinearOrder R]
[IsStrictOrderedRing R]`). Let `P : RootPairing ι R M N` be a root pairing
with finitely many roots (`[Finite ι]`) that is crystallographic
(`[P.IsCrystallographic]`). Let `f : Module.Dual R M` satisfy
`f (P.root i) ≠ 0` for every `i`. Then every `w : P.weylGroup` is the product
of a list of reflections in simple roots:

```lean
∃ x : List (IsAddIndecomposable.baseOf P.root (f : M →+ R)),
  (x.map fun b : IsAddIndecomposable.baseOf P.root (f : M →+ R) =>
    RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P (b : ι)).prod = w
```

Here `IsAddIndecomposable.baseOf P.root (f : M →+ R)` is Mathlib's set of
simple roots relative to `f`: the indices of the positive roots (those with
`0 < f (P.root i)`) that are not the sum of two positive roots. The
lambda's binder is written with its type so that `x.map` maps over the list
of subtype elements. `RootPairing.weylGroup.ofIdx P i` is the reflection in
the `i`-th root as an element of `P.weylGroup`. The theorem adds no
reducedness, spanning or irreducibility hypothesis.

## Provenance and scope

This is an auxiliary module for the proof of
`Langlands.Group.RootPairingWeylCoxeterStatement`
([statement](RootPairingCoxeterStatement.md)), which needs the generation of
the Weyl group by the simple reflections. Generation by simple reflections is
part of the classical theory cited in that task, Bourbaki, *Lie groups and
Lie algebras*, Ch. VI §1.5. The argument below is a standard
minimal-counterexample proof written directly for Lean; no source text is
translated. The pinned Mathlib has the base `baseOf`, the fact that positive
roots lie in the additive monoid generated by the base
(`AddSubmonoid.closure_image_isAddIndecomposable_baseOf`) and linear
independence of the base (`RootPairing.linearIndepOn_root_baseOf'`), but no
generation statement. The module imports only Mathlib.

## Helper lemmas

All helper lemmas are private.

* `ofIdx_reflectionPerm`: for all `b, j`,
  `ofIdx P (P.reflectionPerm b j) = ofIdx P b * ofIdx P j * ofIdx P b`. Both
  sides are elements of the subgroup `P.weylGroup` of `Aut P`. The proof
  compares them through the injective `Equiv.weightHom` and uses Mathlib's
  `RootPairing.reflection_reflectionPerm`. This lemma needs only a
  commutative ring.
* `ofIdx_eq_of_root_eq_smul`: if `P.root j = t • P.root i`, then
  `ofIdx P j = ofIdx P i`. Mathlib's `smul_coroot_eq_of_root_eq_smul` gives
  `t • P.coroot j = P.coroot i`. Then
  `⟨x, P.coroot j⟩ • P.root j = ⟨x, P.coroot i⟩ • P.root i` for every `x`,
  so the two reflections agree on `M`. This lemma uses a field of
  characteristic zero and `Finite ι`.
* `zero_lt_pairing_comm`: `0 < P.pairing i j ↔ 0 < P.pairing j i`, from
  Mathlib's `zero_lt_pairingIn_iff'` over `ℤ`. It uses the
  crystallographic hypothesis.
* `root_mem_closure` and `neg_root_mem_closure`: a positive root, and the
  negative of a negative root, lie in the additive submonoid generated by the
  simple roots. The second applies the first to the root
  `P.root (P.reflectionPerm i i) = -P.root i`.
* `exists_coord`: for a simple index `c` there is a linear form `φ` with
  `φ (P.root c) = 1` and `φ (P.root d) = 0` for the other simple indices `d`.
  By linear independence of the base, `P.root c` is not in the span of the
  other simple roots. `Submodule.exists_dual_map_eq_bot_of_notMem` gives a
  form vanishing on that span and nonzero at `P.root c`, which is then
  rescaled.

## A simple reflection makes only multiples of its root negative

`exists_root_eq_smul_of_reflection`: let `b` be simple and let `P.root i` be
positive with `f (s_b (P.root i)) < 0`, where `s_b = P.reflection b`. Then
`P.root i = t • P.root b` for some `t : R`.

The proof chooses a coordinate form `φ c` (from `exists_coord`) for each
simple `c`. Induction on the additive closure shows that every `x` in the
monoid generated by the simple roots has `φ c x ≥ 0` for all simple `c` and
equals `∑ c, φ c x • P.root c`, the sum over the finite set of simple
indices. Apply this to the positive root `P.root i` and to `-s_b (P.root i)`,
which is the negative of the negative root `P.root (P.reflectionPerm b i)`.
For a simple `c ≠ b`, `φ c (s_b (P.root i)) = φ c (P.root i)` because
`φ c (P.root b) = 0`. So `φ c (P.root i)` is both `≥ 0` and `≤ 0`, and hence
zero. The coordinate expansion of `P.root i` then leaves only the term
`φ b (P.root i) • P.root b`.

## Every positive root pairs positively with a simple coroot

`exists_pairing_pos`: if `P.root i` is positive, then
`0 < P.pairing i b` for some simple `b`. Otherwise, by `zero_lt_pairing_comm`,
`P.pairing b i ≤ 0` for every simple `b`, so the form `P.coroot' i` is `≤ 0`
on every simple root and hence on the monoid they generate. That monoid
contains `P.root i`, but `P.coroot' i (P.root i) = P.pairing i i = 2`.

## Reflections in roots

`exists_list_prod_ofIdx_of_pos`: for a positive root `P.root i`, the
reflection `ofIdx P i` is a product of simple reflections. Suppose not. The
set of indices `k` of positive roots whose reflection is not such a product
is finite and nonempty. `Set.Finite.exists_minimalFor` picks such a `k` with
minimal value `f (P.root k)`. `exists_pairing_pos` gives a simple `b` with
`0 < P.pairing k b`. Let `k' = P.reflectionPerm b k`, so
`P.root k' = P.root k - P.pairing k b • P.root b` and
`f (P.root k') < f (P.root k)` because `0 < f (P.root b)`.

* If `P.root k'` is negative, `exists_root_eq_smul_of_reflection` makes
  `P.root k` a multiple of `P.root b`. By `ofIdx_eq_of_root_eq_smul`, the
  reflection `ofIdx P k` equals `ofIdx P b`, a one-letter product.
* If `P.root k'` is positive, minimality writes `ofIdx P k'` as a product of
  a list `x` of simple reflections. Since `P.reflectionPerm b k' = k`,
  `ofIdx_reflectionPerm` gives
  `ofIdx P k = ofIdx P b * ofIdx P k' * ofIdx P b`, the product of
  `b :: (x ++ [b])`.

Both cases contradict the choice of `k`.

`exists_list_prod_ofIdx` extends this to every index `i`. If `P.root i` is
negative, the root `P.root (P.reflectionPerm i i) = (-1) • P.root i` is
positive and has the same reflection, by `ofIdx_eq_of_root_eq_smul`.

## The theorem

`exists_list_prod_ofIdx_baseOf` uses Mathlib's `RootPairing.weylGroup.induction`
on the subgroup generated by the reflections. A generator `ofIdx P i` is
handled by `exists_list_prod_ofIdx`. The identity is the empty product. If
two elements are the products of lists `a` and `c`, their product is the
product of `a ++ c`. The induction principle has no inverse case.
